candidate_sources.title: Cercospora longipes (brown leaf spot of sugarcane) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Compendium datasheet on Cercospora longipes, the causal agent of brown leaf spot of sugarcane. Includes distribution, host range, symptoms, biology, and management information.

candidate_sources.title: Sugarcane | Texas Plant Disease Handbook
candidate_sources.snippet: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Plant Disease Handbook entry for sugarcane listing major diseases including brown spot (Cercospora longipes), eye spot, leaf scald, red rot, smut, and rust with symptoms and management.

candidate_sources.title: Field Crops: Sugarcane | LSU AgCenter Plant Disease Guide
candidate_sources.snippet: LSU AgCenter plant disease management guide for sugarcane field crops covering brown spot, rust, leaf scald, smut, ratoon stunting, and other diseases with identification and control recommendations for Louisiana.

candidate_sources.title: Sugarcane grassy shoot phytoplasma (grassy shoot of sugarcane) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Compendium datasheet covering Identity, Overview, Distribution, Dispersal, Hosts/Species Affected, Vectors & Intermediate Hosts, Diagnosis, Biology & Ecology, Environmental Requirements, Seedborne Aspects, Impacts, Prevention/Control for sugarcane grassy shoot phytoplasma (16SrXI-B group).

candidate_sources.title: Grassy Shoot of Sugarcane | Pests & Diseases - Plantix
candidate_sources.snippet: Phytoplasma-infected sugarcane plants show proliferation of tillers giving typical grassy appearance. Leaves appear white or creamy yellow. Caused by Candidatus Phytoplasma sacchari. Transmitted via seed material and phloem-feeding leafhopper vectors. Management includes certified disease-free sets and moist hot air treatment.

candidate_sources.title: SUGARCANE :: MAJOR DISEASE :: GRASSY SHOOT - eAgri (TNAU)
candidate_sources.snippet: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University extension page on sugarcane grassy shoot disease. Symptoms include numerous small thin tillers with narrow leaves, albinism, premature excessive tillering giving crowded grass-like appearance, reduced root system, stunted growth. Caused by phytoplasma transmitted by leafhopper vectors.

candidate_sources.title: Sugarcane Leaf Scald - SS-AGR-201/SC001 - University of Florida IFAS Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Detailed extension factsheet covering sugarcane leaf scald caused by Xanthomonas albilineans. Describes symptoms including white pencil line streaks 1-2 mm wide on leaves extending from midrib to margin, diffuse yellow border, necrosis from leaf tip, scalded appearance. Covers latent infections, disease cycle, and management.

candidate_sources.title: Xanthomonas albilineans (leaf scald of sugarcane) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Compendium datasheet for Xanthomonas albilineans, causal agent of sugarcane leaf scald. Covers identity, distribution (confirmed in at least 65 countries), hosts/species affected, diagnosis, biology & ecology, impacts, and prevention/control. First reported in 1911 in Australia.

candidate_sources.title: Sugarcane Diseases: Gummosis and Leaf Scald | USDA APHIS
candidate_sources.snippet: USDA Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service page on sugarcane diseases including leaf scald caused by Xanthomonas albilineans. Covers regulatory significance, symptoms, pathogen biology, and USDA management/quarantine measures for sugarcane leaf scald and gummosis.

candidate_sources.title: Sugarcane Pokkah Boeng Disease: Insights and Future Directions for Effective Management
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive review covering Pokkah Boeng caused by Fusarium species complex (F. sacchari, F. verticillioides, F. proliferatum, F. incarnatum, F. andiyazi). Symptoms include chlorotic phase, top rot phase, knife cut phase, ladder-like lesions, twisted leaves, and malformed shoot. Disease is airborne, emerges during hot humid conditions. Management includes resistant varieties, fungicide applications (carbendazim, copper oxychloride, mancozeb), and removal of symptomatic canes. Yield losses of 10-38% reported.

candidate_sources.title: Pokkah Boeng | Pests & Diseases - Plantix
candidate_sources.snippet: Practical disease guide for Pokkah Boeng of sugarcane. Covers symptoms (chlorosis, leaf distortion, knife-cut lesions on stalks, top rot), causal pathogen Fusarium moniliforme (Gibberella fujikuroi), favorable conditions (hot and humid weather during rapid growth), and integrated management recommendations including cultural practices and chemical control.

candidate_sources.title: Identification and Characterization of Pathogenic and Endophytic Fungal Species Associated with Pokkah Boeng Disease of Sugarcane
candidate_sources.snippet: Peer-reviewed research identifying five Fusarium species as causal agents of Pokkah Boeng disease: F. incarnatum, F. andiyazi, F. sacchari, F. proliferatum, and F. verticillioides. Details pathogen characterization, molecular identification, and pathogenicity testing on sugarcane. Published in Pathogens (2017).

candidate_sources.title: Sett rot - TNAU Agritech Portal
candidate_sources.snippet: Sett rot caused by Ceratocystis paradoxa. The affected tissues first develop a reddish colour which turns to brownish black in later stages. Severely affected setts show internodal cavities covered with mycelium and abundant spores. A characteristic pineapple smell is associated with the rotting tissues.

candidate_sources.title: Fact sheet - Sugarcane pineapple disease (218) - Pacific Pests, Pathogens, Weeds & Pesticides
candidate_sources.snippet: Pineapple disease caused by Ceratocystis paradoxa in sugarcane. In sugarcane, pineapple disease causes reddening of internal sett tissues with black centres containing spores. Cavities develop where fungus produces spores; roots fail to form, buds fail to grow, and those that do die back or remain stunted. Cultural and chemical control described.

candidate_sources.title: Surveying Potential Soilborne Pathogens Causing Sett Rot on Sugarcane in Southern Florida | Plant Disease
candidate_sources.snippet: Surveys during 2023 and 2024 planting seasons identified Thielaviopsis sp. and Fusarium sp. in 43 and 38% of 569 sampled seed cane, respectively. Thielaviopsis ethacetica identified as etiological agent of sugarcane pineapple sett rot disease.

candidate_sources.title: Sugarcane streak mosaic virus | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Compendium datasheet covering Sugarcane streak mosaic virus (SCSMV): identity, distribution, hosts/species affected, diagnosis, biology & ecology, impact, associated diseases, dispersal, environmental requirements, and management. Comprehensive reference for this Poacevirus in family Potyviridae.

candidate_sources.title: Historical Review of Sugarcane Streak Mosaic Virus that Has Recently Emerged in Africa | Phytopathology
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive historical review of SCSMV (genus Poacevirus, family Potyviridae), first reported 1932 in Louisiana. Covers symptoms (irregular yellow-green mosaic, interveinal chlorotic specks and streaks), diagnosis (DAS-ELISA, RT-PCR), yield losses (30% in non-irrigated fields in Côte d'Ivoire), and management including hot water treatment at 53°C for 10 min and genetic resistance.

candidate_sources.title: Sugarcane Mosaic Disease: Characteristics, Identification and Control
candidate_sources.snippet: Peer-reviewed review covering sugarcane mosaic diseases including SCSMV and SCMV. Describes symptoms: chlorotic streaks parallel to midrib, flecks, mottling, stunted growth, systemic yellowing and marginal leaf drying in susceptible genotypes. Covers PCR-based diagnostics (RT-PCR, qRT-PCR), epidemiology, and integrated disease management strategies.

candidate_sources.title: Sugarcane mosaic virus (sugarcane mosaic) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive datasheet covering Identity, Overview, Distribution, Dispersal, Hosts/Species Affected, Vectors & Intermediate Hosts, Diagnosis, Biology & Ecology, Seedborne Aspects, Impacts, Prevention/Control of Sugarcane mosaic virus.

candidate_sources.title: Sugarcane Mosaic Disease: Characteristics, Identification and Control
candidate_sources.snippet: Review covering the SCMV complex consisting of four distinct potyviruses including strains of Johnsongrass mosaic virus (JGMV), maize dwarf mosaic virus (MDMV), sorghum mosaic virus (SrMV), and SCMV. Discusses symptoms including mosaic patterns of light green to yellow patches on normal green colour, chlorotic or necrotic streaks parallel to veins, and management through resistant varieties.

candidate_sources.title: PP313/PP313: Mosaic Disease of St. Augustinegrass Caused by Sugarcane Mosaic Virus
candidate_sources.snippet: UF/IFAS Extension factsheet on Sugarcane Mosaic Virus. Covers symptoms including intense mottling, broken yellow streaks between veins, growth stunting, and necrosis. Details mechanical transmission via equipment and aphid vectors. Management includes resistant varieties, equipment sanitation with dilute bleach or quaternary ammonia.

candidate_sources.title: Present Status and Future Management Strategies for Sugarcane Yellow Leaf Virus: A Major Constraint to the Global Sugarcane Production
candidate_sources.snippet: Sugarcane yellow leaf virus (SCYLV) is one of the most widespread viruses causing disease in sugarcane worldwide. Infection results in intense yellowing of the midrib extending to the leaf blade, followed by tissue necrosis from leaf tip towards the base. The virus has been responsible for drastic economic losses in most sugarcane-growing regions.

candidate_sources.title: Yellow Leaf Disease Management in Sugarcane: Symptoms, Identification, Treatment, Chemical, Biological, Natural, and Organic Control
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive guide covering yellow leaf disease symptoms, identification, and treatment including chemical, biological, natural, and organic control methods for sugarcane yellow leaf virus (ScYLV) transmitted by aphid vector Melanaphis sacchari.

candidate_sources.title: Biology and management of sugarcane yellow leaf virus: an historical overview
candidate_sources.snippet: Historical overview of SCYLV biology and management. Covers transmission by Melanaphis sacchari in circulative non-propagative manner, symptom expression including midrib yellowing and necrosis, and management through meristem tip culture and resistant varieties.

candidate_sources.title: Passalora koepkei (yellow spot of sugarcane) | Plantwise Knowledge Bank
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Compendium datasheet for Passalora koepkei, the causal agent of yellow spot disease of sugarcane. Previously known as Mycovellosiella koepkei and Cercospora koepkei. Covers distribution, symptoms, pathogen biology, and management.

candidate_sources.title: Sugarcane | Diseases and Pests, Description, Uses, Propagation - PlantVillage (Penn State)
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive university guide covering major sugarcane diseases and pests including yellow spot, brown spot, eye spot, red rot, smut, rust, and leaf scald. Includes symptom descriptions, pathogen information, and management recommendations.

candidate_sources.title: Integrated Disease Management of Sugarcane | LSU AgCenter
candidate_sources.snippet: LSU AgCenter extension publication on integrated disease management of sugarcane covering major diseases in Louisiana including brown rust, orange rust, smut, leaf scald, yellow leaf, brown stripe, ring spot, and yellow spot. Includes symptoms, pathogen details, and management strategies.
